Source Code Snippet: PluginInterfaceRef& operator=(PluginInterfaceRef&& other) { if (this != &other) { _interface = other._interface; other._interface = nullptr; } return *this; }
Issue Description: The move-assignment operator overwrites an existing interface pointer without releasing it and does not transfer the paired controller pointer, which can leak a reference and leave stale state behind.
Suggested Fix: Release any currently held interface before assignment and move both _interface and _service from the source object.
Resolution Status and Notes: Fixed - move assignment now resets the current interface before transfer and moves the controller pointer alongside the interface.

Source Code Snippet: char* error = strdup(message.c_str()); t2_event_s((char *)"THUNDER_ERROR", error); if (error) { free(error); }
Issue Description: sendError passes the strdup result to t2_event_s before verifying allocation succeeded, so an allocation failure would pass a null pointer into the telemetry API.
Suggested Fix: Check the duplicated buffer for null before calling t2_event_s and free it only after successful use.
Resolution Status and Notes: Fixed - telemetry emission now occurs only when strdup succeeds, preventing a null buffer from reaching t2_event_s.

Issue Description: The active configuration descriptor returned by libusb_get_active_config_descriptor is never released on the success path, leaking descriptor memory during GetDeviceInfo processing.
Suggested Fix: Free config_desc with libusb_free_config_descriptor after reading bmAttributes.
Resolution Status and Notes: Fixed - the successful active-config path now releases config_desc immediately after reading bmAttributes.

Source Code Snippet: status = ...getUSBDeviceInfoStructFromDeviceDescriptor(...); if (Core::ERROR_NONE != status) { deviceInfo.deviceLevel = libusb_get_port_numbers(...); ... } else { LOGWARN("getUSBDeviceInfoStructFromDeviceDescriptor Failed"); }
Issue Description: GetDeviceInfo inverts the success check after getUSBDeviceInfoStructFromDeviceDescriptor, so parentId and deviceLevel are derived only on failure while successful calls incorrectly log a failure warning.
Suggested Fix: Flip the condition so parent traversal runs only when descriptor extraction succeeds and keep the warning path for real failures.
Resolution Status and Notes: Fixed - the success check now uses Core::ERROR_NONE so parentId and deviceLevel are computed only after successful descriptor extraction.
